note.question: When should a firm buy an input from a downstream competitor rather than an outside supplier, given that doing so softens price competition but exposes innovation to spillover and future holdup?
note.overview: A focal firm chooses whether to source from a downstream competitor or an outside supplier, bargains over a two-part tariff, competes in prices, and makes a noncontractible investment whose knowledge may spill over to its supplier-competitor. The paper solves the repeated bargaining and downstream-competition game by backward induction.

components.label: Model sequence and system structure
components.explanation: In each of two periods, firm A chooses whether to source from competitor S or outside supplier T. When A sources from S, A and S negotiate a two-part tariff through equal-weight Nash bargaining and then A and S set downstream prices simultaneously. In period 1, A can make a supplier-specific, noncontractible investment before the relevant pricing interaction; that investment raises A's second-period value and may spill over to S. The second-period sourcing, bargaining, and pricing game then repeats.
